subject: Uplift de-risk: proposed credit + deploy timing
messages:
From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@novamed.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal roadmap & mid-year uplift

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the call this morning. To summarize Novamed's ask: we expect a 35% uplift in token usage starting mid-July as we bring two new features online. Procurement is looking to avoid a multi-month budget surprise and would like two things from Redwood before we commit: 1) a short-term credit to cover deployment risk while usage ramps (we suggested a $50k risk pool) and 2) a clear deployment timetable tied to pricing (we need guarantees around latency and an option to fall back to a cheaper quantized variant if cost spikes).

Attached is a short spreadsheet with projected monthly token growth and current PO cadence (Novamed_Uplift_Requests_3.30.xlsx).

Can you propose a simple structure we can take to legal and finance? We prefer something concise — an amendment or short addendum with explicit credit mechanics.

Best,
Lina Gomez
Director, Platform Integrations
Novamed

Attachments: Novamed_Uplift_Requests_3.30.xlsx (spreadsheet, 32 KB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@novamed.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal roadmap & mid-year uplift

Lina —

Thanks for the clear summary and the model. I reviewed the sheet and sketched a straightforward path that should satisfy procurement and keep ops comfortable:

- Short amendment (1 page) that:
  • Creates a "deployment credit" of $50,000 mapped to July–Sept 2027 token overage;
  • Credits are drawn down only if usage exceeds the committed baseline and are applied as one-off invoice credits;
  • If total usage exceeds a 60% increase vs baseline, we trigger an optional fallback to a quantized model for non-sensitive routes (configurable per route).
- Pricing: we propose a temporary uplift rate of 12% on top of current unit price for the three-month ramp window; the deployment credit offsets the uplift for the first 6M tokens over baseline.
- SLA tie: we can commit to regional latency targets for your production region (US-west) and provide a 30-day rollback window if performance or cost profile isn't acceptable.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Kimberly and Ben, can you review the credit language and produce a clean amendment draft and a redlined SOW (SOW_draft_v1.pdf) we can share with Novamed legal?
2) Lina, if that structure looks directionally right I can put together a short one-page summary for your CFO and procurement and we can run this as an amendment (no full contract rewrite).

Happy to jump on a quick call with procurement if that helps.

—Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW_draft_v1.pdf (PDF, 18 KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@novamed.com>, Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal roadmap & mid-year uplift — draft pricing options

Rishi / Ben / Lina —

I put together two compact options based on our pricing playbook: one-credit (minimal ops) and two-credit (more protective for Novamed). See summary below and updated spreadsheet attached.

Option A — Single deployment credit (preferred, simpler)
- $50k one-time credit applied to July–Sept overage;
- Temporary uplift rate: +12% for the ramp window;
- Fallback: route-level switch to quantized variant if 60% threshold hit;
- No change to renewal term; amendment captures credit mechanics.

Option B — Staged credit + consumption floor (more conservative)
- $30k immediate credit + $25k contingency pool (total $55k);
- Consumption floor: Novamed pays at least 90% of the committed baseline each month; credits only apply after floor is met;
- Discount on quantized variant (if used) set at -8% to encourage fallback usage;
- Requires a brief amendment and a one-paragraph procurement addendum.

Operational notes:
- I flagged the routes Lina mentioned as "sensitive" — fallback won't be available for those.
- Legal will want explicit drawdown mechanics; I recommend we keep it invoice-credit based to avoid complicated escrow.

I've attached an updated workbook (Novamed_Uplift_Requests_3.30.xlsx) with the two scenarios and simple monthly cashflow. If Novamed prefers Option B we'll need procurement to confirm the floor language.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Pricing Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Novamed_Uplift_Requests_3.30.xlsx (updated, 45 KB)

Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal roadmap & mid-year uplift — exec signoff path

Lina —

Appreciate the model and the flexibility. I'm happy to confirm we can move forward with Option A as a standard approach, with a small ask: if Novamed signs the amendment by Apr 15 we can expand the deployment credit to $60k (adds $10k in contingent protection) and lock the temporary uplift rate at +10% (down from 12%). That concession is tied to an exec approval window for our finance team.

If that sounds reasonable, Rishi please prepare the one-page summary for Novamed CFO and add the Apr 15 milestone in the amendment draft. Kimberly — can you incorporate the milestone / escalator language and prepare a redline for legal?

Lina — once we have a quick yes to the milestone we'll route the amendment through legal and finance and aim to have signatures within 10 business days.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
